package_info.package_name: Unknown (malicious NPM package referenced in campaign)
package_info.why_malicious: The package acts as a first-stage malware downloader, designed to fetch and execute additional payloads from remote servers. It is distributed via social engineering, targeting developers in high-value sectors, and is part of a sophisticated supply-chain attack attributed to the Lazarus Group.

execution_context.trigger: import-time or runtime (when the package is loaded or executed as part of the project)
execution_context.file_location: main JavaScript file of the malicious npm package

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Disables TLS certificate validation, checks for a hidden directory in the user's home folder, reads a token from a file, and sends it to a remote server (bi2price.com) via a custom function, likely exfiltrating sensitive data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code disables TLS security, accesses hidden files in the user's home directory, and exfiltrates data to an external domain. These are classic indicators of credential theft or data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages should not disable TLS validation, read hidden tokens, or send user data to unknown external servers without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software might read configuration files or tokens, but would not disable TLS or exfiltrate data to untrusted domains.
key_indicators: Access to hidden directory and token file in user's home directory
No user interaction or consent for data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Target is socially engineered to install or collaborate on a project using the malicious npm package.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious npm package is installed on the developer's machine.

attack_chain.action: Malicious npm package executes code at import-time or runtime, searching for specific files and tokens.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data (token) is read from the filesystem.

attack_chain.action: Sensitive token is exfiltrated to a remote attacker-controlled server (bi2price.com).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives exfiltrated data and may deliver second-stage payloads.

attack_chain.action: Second-stage payload (not captured in analysis) is dynamically delivered and executed, enabling further compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full device compromise, data theft, or further malware installation.

behavioral_signatures: Disabling TLS certificate validation in Node.js processes
Access to hidden directories and files in user home directories (e.g., /.cprice, /pricetoken)
Outbound network requests to suspicious or newly registered domains during package installation or execution
Unexpected file reads and exfiltration at import-time or runtime
file_indicators: References to bi2price.com or similar domains in package code
network_indicators: Any network activity to domains listed in GitHub's published IoCs for this campaign
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for code that disables TLS validation, accesses hidden files in user directories, or makes outbound requests to suspicious domains. Flag packages that read tokens or credentials and immediately send them to external servers. Use threat intelligence feeds to block or alert on known malicious domains and IoCs associated with Lazarus campaigns.
